The configured immutable source is
6a85c31011b7a1ca23d745e9868d7b01dd0e92e9fe74c997e8222482f76393ca.
Eight independently qualified H200 verifier workers share the existing queue;
the validator/controller remains on Arbos.life, with separate miner, trainer
and evaluator roles. No hardware outside its admitted runtime is approved.

The new contract uses small-commitment-pairs-v2 token-document transport and
committed-unaudited-training-v1. Cheap-admitted immutable checkpoint-bound
training documents can enter training without waiting for expensive audits.
This labels training inputs UNAUDITED; it does not claim they all passed proof
verification. Continuous auditors independently select committed batches,
verify selected proof artifacts, native environment outcomes and target-model
computation, and publish authenticated reports. Historical signed epochs keep
their original strict sampler, training and reward contracts.

Sampling verification is forced-inverse-cdf-prefill-support-v3 with an approved
FP32 H200 inference profile. TOPLOC fingerprints alone do not prove sampling.
The verifier recomputes target-model probabilities and checks the forced random
draw against calibrated CDF intervals; numerical ambiguity or support changes
require exact cached-reference replay. Unavailable reference computation is
unknown, not fraud. Calibrated numerical bounds and random audits provide
empirical/probabilistic assurance, not an exact universal proof of historical
execution. Trainer BF16 precision is separately admitted. The config retains
its predecessor calibration seed only to reuse original qualification requests;
each opened manifest must use the actual checkpoint-specific admitted policy.
Successor checkpoints require fresh executed qualification before opening.

Continuous-probabilistic-audit-v2 rewards unique eligible task indices adjusted
by authenticated audit evidence. It uses eight recent cohorts, decay 0.8 and
Beta(1,1), with confirmed-invalid multiplier 0.1, zero epoch after two confirmed
invalids, and four-epoch blacklist after three. Infrastructure failures and
numerical unknowns are not fraud. Eight inflight jobs and eight selections per
10-second tick bound audit load. Four parallel storage-capture threads preserve
every committed draw, conditional object copy and complete SHA check; queue and
authority journals remain serialized. Fresh job TTL starts after capture, while
original job envelopes and expiries are never extended. Hourly immutable snapshots use original
completion times and evidence cutoffs. Extra rollouts on one task earn no extra
points; same-epoch task duplicates earn zero. The signed contracts are the
source of truth for eligibility and penalties. Lossless DEFLATE level one is
configured for new proof artifacts; historical artifact bytes are unchanged.

The independently signed operator execution-evidence policy took effect
at the 2026-10-05 17:00 UTC hourly cutoff. For the exact approved standard backend,
source inventory, FP32 profile and runtime pins, the immutable verifier report
must truthfully retain execution_resources_enforced=false: this backend does
not implement the separate long-context OS resource enforcement. False does
not mean failed model verification. No report is rewritten to true, and unknown
sources/profiles or forged flags are rejected. Other backend contracts keep
their required true enforcement flag. Original report signatures, model/source,
checkpoint, TOPLOC, sampler and grading checks remain required. The new signed
snapshots explicitly disclaim OS enforcement and proof of historical execution;
earlier snapshots and historical signed contracts are unchanged.

Qualification evidence: eight distinct H200s passed sixteen honest cached
reference controls and rejected sixteen freshly fingerprinted forged controls.
Fifteen honest prefill controls verified directly and one required numerical
adjudication. The final ambiguity fallback passed its separate honest/forged
controls. Two actual CP05de qualification jobs passed and their signed admission
was verified before deployment. The E15 manifest pins its own CP76bc
checkpoint-specific calibration. These controls do not establish convergence,
a one-hour completed epoch, or universal cross-hardware compatibility.

## Sampling cutover

Cutover state: sampling enforcement began with epoch nonpayable-live-reward-math-v1--1791128338-9. The current native-grader, compact-input and persistent-optimizer contract is active from epoch nonpayable-live-reward-math-v1--1791154261-10. Check mining.json and the signed manifest for current upload availability.

The current immutable source bundle is SHA256 5bcb01b6ca4187e6dce785c67256688faa950058c39dc7db70ce5b24e03e016f, admitted on all seven role machines. E10 used historical source7630e0d25f388fe480341614c861fa5be1650f110b49e343dc9134c05e492ab0; those jobs are unchanged. It preserves the forced-sampler computation and adds pinned native grading, authenticated-verifier-compact-inputs-v2 and persistent FP32 training. Historical E9 inference used e415623e5a8017133ff7bef3925b724441862f34b6d034ed0deb6b731a26e657; its receipt trainer used 94ff74eb335e24d4702da2ec10cc0aee068076b003e6c0b13b0e81f5090bc79c. Every epoch's signed manifest and source are authoritative. GitHub main may contain prospective optimizations; do not substitute a checkout for the signed bundle. mining.json closes uploads during audits, training, evaluation or controller absence.

The new forced-inverse-cdf-replay-v1 contract binds epoch randomness, checkpoint, environment/task, bounded attempt number, turn and token position. Miner identity does not change the draws. The signed attempt budget is 128: attempt numbers 0 through 127. Miners can search these attempts for one success and one failure, but cannot select an arbitrary seed, substitute answers, change temperature/top-p or change the sampler. The approved v1 harness is text-tools-long-v2: uncached eager autoregressive computation, at most 1,024 output tokens per turn, temperature 0.8 and top-p 1. The signed manifest and source take precedence over this guide.

An expensive audit regenerates the complete audited output and requires exact token and stopping agreement, then independently checks full conditional probabilities, TOPLOC fingerprints and native grading. Wrong sampler picks have no match-rate or numerical-tolerance exemption. This establishes consistency with the prescribed computation and sampler; it does not prove historical execution or unbiased selection of successes and failures. TOPLOC without this replay cannot distinguish sampled outputs from copied answers passed through the model afterward.

Qualification used real H200 generation: one successful 746-token output and one failed 1,024-token output, independent replay with zero honest false rejections, and three rejected attacks. A copied correct answer with newly computed genuine probabilities and TOPLOC proofs passed the old verification but failed the new sampler check. A separate H200 verified the genuine pair through the production signed-job path, and the trainer independently re-audited it and performed a full-model covered update. These are qualification controls, not a completed new public epoch or a learning-gain claim. Details: https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine/blob/main/docs/FORCED_SAMPLING_QUALIFICATION.md

Epoch eight completed under its original rules; its final training was explicitly skipped after a disk-capacity refusal. E9 then completed three covered-v3 updates and published checkpoint 28d478ac16c36fb0ab816f0273aee220e42927136c1e5a8ee3c34792b6d38384. E10 begins from that checkpoint with an explicitly authorized persistent-optimizer genesis at step zero. Historical updates and private qualification steps are not persistent public optimizer counters. Old manifests, scores, evidence and writer history are preserved. The old burn and equal-registration writers remain disabled; the single guarded reward writer uses the signed policy for all eligible registered subnet identities.

## Model and taskset

Qwen/Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct has 7,615,616,512 parameters. Inference weights and GPU forward/backward use BF16; the current full-model optimizer retains FP32 masters and AdamW moments across epochs. The active original MATH taskset contains 7,496 distinct usable problems: 6,746 mining tasks and 750 reserved held-out tasks. DeepMath and NuminaMath are not yet part of this contract. K=1 and L=1: one genuinely graded success and one genuinely graded failure for the same task on the approved checkpoint.

Held-out evaluation retains the precommitted sampler and fixed task/seed identities, so contract upgrades do not redefine the measurement. Its outputs cannot supply mining evidence. E9's matched 32-task diagnostic changed from 20/32 before to 19/32 after; this does not show improvement. An independently authenticated CP093 baseline solved 141/200 reserved tasks. The precommitted larger comparison waits for three nonempty public persistent-v4 epochs and uses those same 200 tasks. Private optimizer qualification is not public training progress or convergence.

## How to start mining

Use a coding agent to read this guide and the repository guides, set up your
miner, watch discovery and diagnose failures. Keep watching this document and
GitHub main: fixes and upgrades will continue. Each epoch's signed source and
checkpoint take precedence over an older checkout. Never silently reuse an old
source, upload grant, deadline or model checkpoint.

Admission is open to every current subnet-120 identity with valid signed Affine
Ed25519 activation. There is no operator whitelist. Each epoch snapshots the
eligible identities; later activations enter a subsequent epoch. The signed
current manifest contains the actual eligible identity snapshot. Registration/activation is
separate from public dashboard access. Keep signing keys private.

Start with these concrete guides:
- https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine/blob/main/docs/MINER_QUICKSTART.md
- https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine/blob/main/docs/MATH_MINER_BOOTSTRAP.md
- https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine/blob/main/docs/DISTRIBUTED_GPU_ROLES.md
- https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine/blob/main/docs/FORCED_SAMPLING_CUTOVER.md

Use the exact runtime and hardware profile pinned in the signed manifest.
H200/SM90, CUDA BF16 eager, disabled TF32 and CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8
are the qualified profile. Core version pins are torch 2.14.0, transformers
5.14.1 and toploc 0.1.6. A package version alone does not qualify a different
GPU/runtime; follow the full setup/profile instructions. The manifest's numerical
policy is authoritative. Full output probability width is 152,064, distinct from
the tokenizer's 151,665 entries.

Read authority and current_url from https://affine.io/mining.json. Run the signed
source bootstrap using your private activated Ed25519 seed file:

CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8 python -B -m subnet.source_bootstrap \
  --authority "$AFFINE_OPERATOR_AUTHORITY" \
  --current-url "$AFFINE_SIGNED_CURRENT_URL" \
  --source-cache /absolute/private/source-cache \
  --key /absolute/private/miner.key \
  --state /absolute/private/miner-state \
  --env-id affine_math --max-batches 3 --search-budget 8 --once

The search budget is a local per-task choice, not the signed attempt ceiling.
Start with eight attempts per task, then move on if no success/failure pair is
found. Using all 128 attempts on a consistently solved or consistently failed
task can consume the epoch without completing a batch. Budgets from one through
128 are supported; smaller budgets do not change the model, public draws,
temperature, proof checks or the three-batch quota.

The authority public key is
3301134b38401196d006a621ac4a772bb4b0e6afa15a7d34a0d1ae5f2c630bcd.
The bootstrap authenticates the signed pointer/manifest, approved source archive
and checkpoint file hashes. It admits the original task snapshot and executes
that signed code. Source approval authorizes execution; it is not a sandbox.
Your agent should monitor new epochs and launch each only once, inspect original
process handles after faults and never restart solely because observation timed
out. Do not share your wallet key, decrypted private upload capability or R2
credentials. Miners need no permanent bucket credentials.

## Batch and reward rules

The current signed quota is three batches per UID per epoch, with artifact-size and rollout limits enforced independently. This is a conservative configurable pilot cap, not a protocol maximum. A batch covers one authorized mining task index on one epoch/checkpoint and includes complete input/output token contexts, full conditional log probabilities, TOPLOC fingerprints, native observations/outcomes, immutable task/model/source identities, and, for new-contract rollouts, the sampler receipt. Extra rollouts on the same task add no points. Grader errors and unsuccessful searches are not valid negative samples.

The active small-commitment-pairs-v1 transport uploads each proof pair to one private slot, then PUTs the signed cumulative commitment last using encrypted per-identity presigned capabilities. Already acknowledged pairs are reused without recompression. Replacements reuse the same three slots. Only completed in-window objects named by the final valid commitment are frozen. Legacy single-object transport is used only if an older signed manifest explicitly requests it. Upload deadlines are not extended to rescue a worker. Frozen artifacts and authenticated audit history are published for inspection; miners do not need permanent R2 credentials.

Cheap bounded structure and quota checks apply to every submission. Expensive audits use the signed random allocation, minimum/maximum per identity, total budget and escalation rules. Reports bind the frozen batch hash, signed original request, approved source, exact checkpoint and winning job lease. Infrastructure faults trigger retries rather than fraud penalties. Only fully audited valid pairs earn points or enter training; observed cross-miner duplicate task keys receive zero for all competing miners. Unchecked duplicate claims remain unresolved and that limitation is recorded.

The active bounded-random-v1 policy sets invalid_batch_multiplier=0 and zero_epoch_after=1: one confirmed invalid audited batch zeros the miner's epoch score. With no confirmed invalids, its points are its distinct fully verified accepted task indices. Structural failures earn no batch points but do not multiply remaining points (penalize_structural=false). Unselected, deferred and infrastructure-failed batches earn no verified points and are not invalid samples. Historical manifests retain their original penalty rules. Penalties reduce rewards; they do not take wallet funds. Exact adjusted points are summed over finalized epochs in the completed UTC hour and normalized across currently eligible owners. The writer waits for pending audits/final scores before closing their hour and does not treat unresolved work as zero. Every policy change applies prospectively through a signed manifest.

## Independent roles and durable history

Arbos.life is the operator host running the validator/controller, authenticated audit queue, single chain writer, discovery monitor and dashboard. The active GPU roles are one owned test miner, four independent verifiers, one trainer and one evaluator on seven existing Lium role endpoints. A qualified optimizer reader runs on a separate retained physical host and does not require GPU numerical qualification. Only the four approved verifier identities may serve E12; unqualified hardware and deleted or retired workers are not silently admitted. Shared R2 stores signed manifests, frozen submissions, reports, scores, checkpoints and history. This dashboard is at affine.io; the Arbos website and DNS are unchanged.

Verifier nodes lease jobs and publish authenticated results. Four verifier workers run approved E12 sourcea65d7ed8 in parallel; they retain their existing identities and queue history. E9 completed 183 distinct gradient pairs over three updates, produced CP28, and passed full R2 publication readback. Its historical 20/32 to 19/32 evaluation remains visible. In E10, the coordinator derives canonical accepted batch documents only from original COMPLETE jobs and authenticated worker report requests. The trainer authenticates the nested audit receipts and exact canonical tokens/outcomes, without repeating inference, TOPLOC, sampler or environment verification. Original proof ZIPs remain durable in R2. Reports distinguish training admissions from audits and explicitly record trainer_verification_performed=false. Authenticated audit points and configured penalties determine normalized proposed rewards; new-source authorization preserves historical E9 signatures.

Historical E9 used an explicit signed training amendment binding its accepted receipts to the original three-update covered-v3 objective. It is complete and is not rewritten as a persistent epoch. Historical E10 used source763 consistently across miner, verifier, trainer, evaluator and coordinator, with a separate signed additive reward-source authorization. This preserves old signed cutover documents and authorizes the four existing verifier identities only for the new source.

After admission, E11 configures one full-model update over accepted audited pairs against the fixed input-checkpoint reference and publishes one immutable successor checkpoint plus sharded FP32 optimizer state. The next epoch waits for verification, actual training and durable publication. Matched held-out evaluation runs independently on its dedicated machine; it cannot supply training evidence. Persistent-v4 requires the authority-committed latest parent and monotonically increasing optimizer counters, even if a small update leaves the BF16 inference hash unchanged. Missing or corrupted state cannot silently reset the optimizer. Mining can open while completed-download retention runs; actual training must pass its current RAM/disk/GPU admission. A configured step count is not a completed update or learning-gain claim.

Automatic completed-download retention keeps R2 and original reports intact and removes only authenticated, completed local submission replicas after complete archive hash/size readback. It does not claim automatic retirement of every old model cache. Extra machines retained for independent qualification are outside the five live role nodes; this guide does not expand hardware approval to them.

The dashboard has two charts: matched held-out math performance over time and frozen submitted batches per finalized epoch. Submitted counts include rejected and unchecked batches; tooltips distinguish accepted totals. It displays observed results, not promised improvements.

Technical references:
- https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine/blob/main/docs/FORCED_SAMPLING_CUTOVER.md
- https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine/blob/main/docs/FORCED_SAMPLING_QUALIFICATION.md
- https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine/blob/main/docs/COVERED_EPOCH_TRAINING.md
- https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine/blob/main/docs/AUDIT_SAMPLING.md
- https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine/blob/main/docs/LIVE_REWARDS.md
- https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine/blob/main/docs/SUBMISSION_RETENTION.md

When reporting failures, provide the epoch, approved source/checkpoint, public UID and sanitized logs. Keep wallet keys, upload grants and credentials private.

Prospective optimization, not the active contract: `docs/FULL_FORWARD_SAMPLER_QUALIFICATION.md` describes a public robust-CDF gate using independently recomputed causal full-forward conditionals. A short private H200 diagnostic passed a genuine 128-token control and rejected a synthetic trajectory with recomputed valid probabilities/TOPLOC. The B200, L40S and RTX4090 short cross-hardware controls completed but failed the pinned probability comparison and remain unqualified. Production qualification is still pending; miners must continue to follow the signed current epoch contract.

## Compact training transport

E10 activates authenticated-verifier-compact-inputs-v2. The coordinator derives canonical accepted batch documents from original COMPLETE verifier jobs, durably reads them back and signs a compact receipt nesting the unchanged original ZIP admission. The trainer receives those exact documents rather than downloading proof arrays again; original ZIPs and full verification history remain in R2. The objective and sampler verification are unchanged. The measured E9 population would use about 8.3 MB of compact frames instead of 78.7 GB of trainer ZIP downloads; this is a transport-size estimate, not an E10 elapsed-time result. Details: https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine/blob/main/docs/COMPACT_TRAINING_INPUTS_V2.md

## Native MATH grading

E10 activates native-math-grader-pinned-indeterminate-v1 with environment source hash 1d1446b678abcffd818318a2e6e3d90a74341a628fbde1fdd9da5ce2b91a4947. Historical E9 grading is preserved. The older grader could classify parsing/comparison timeouts as zero. The current grader classifies timeouts, missing references, runtime mismatches, malformed/nonfinite/out-of-domain results and execution faults as indeterminate. These do not qualify as failure samples and do not trigger fraud penalties. Completed native correct and incorrect answers retain scores one and zero.

The signed environment binds approved Python 3.12.3 interpreter/stdlib profiles, exact grader dependency inventories, isolated import rules and helper source. Use its pinned environment and deployment instructions: unqualified interpreter or dependency builds can produce indeterminate grading. All seven roles passed actual native-grader and compact/trainer integration controls before E10 activation. Details: https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine/blob/main/docs/NATIVE_MATH_GRADER_SECURITY.md

## Prospective miner timing

GitHub main adds a private, bounded epoch-and-identity progress sidecar for the
next approved source. It records task/attempt timing, outcome counts and completed
batch counts, without response text, tokens, arrays, proofs, keys or upload URLs.
Observation write failures do not change mining. E11 source includes bounded
phase telemetry; miners must keep using the signed source. Progress counters never
replace an uploaded artifact, authenticated audit or reward evidence.

E11 approved owned-miner implementation:
bounded-round-robin-v1 searches at most eight active tasks, two attempts per
sweep, preserving original per-task seeds and signed attempt limits. Canonical
pair ZIPs are prepared in one pass with byte-identical framing; already
acknowledged pairs are reused. Both independent-pair sums and hypothetical
cumulative ZIP raw/compressed sizes must fit the existing signed cumulative
artifact limits. The commitment remains signed and PUT last. No proof, sampler
or scoring rule changes. Safe phase telemetry contains counts/timings only.
See docs/BOUNDED_MINER_SEARCH_AND_ONE_PASS_UPLOAD.md on GitHub. Historical sealed
sources and their outcomes are unchanged. E11 generation and upload are observed;
its post-freeze audit and training outcomes must be verified separately.

E11 public Miner transport: small-commitment pairs are compressed once and
cached immutably; legacy cumulative ZIP state is migrated once. The existing
local state filename becomes a private prepared-miner-pairs-v1 JSON index with
adjacent <state-name>.pairs/ SHA-addressed artifacts. Restart verifies full
artifact hashes and original epoch/checkpoint/source/sampling-contract binding,
then reuses exact bytes without recompression. Existing acknowledgements skip
old slot PUTs; signed commitment publication remains last. Legacy transport is
unchanged. Local state contains epoch rollouts; epoch publication rules are unchanged.
This transport is admitted in the signed E11 source. Upload acknowledgments
do not establish an accepted audit or completed training update.

## Prospective optimizer transfer acceleration

The signed bounded-parallel-fp32-state-v1 policy supports one through four
streams. A separate bounded-eight-fp32-state-v1 policy explicitly requests
eight streams; it is never inferred from a worker count or enabled by default.
Both retain full FP32 masters and AdamW moments, exact shard hashes and
restored-buffer checks. Optimizer-state authority publication still waits for
complete independent readback. These transport choices do not change the
sampler, proof checks, training objective or reward eligibility.

The production-sized four-stream CPU control published and read back all
91,387,491,264 bytes in 1,209 seconds, restored them in 488 seconds, and passed
exact restored-buffer comparisons. This isolated zero-gradient control is
transport evidence, not a trained production epoch or convergence result.
An isolated eight-stream CPU control completed all 23 exact shard comparisons and restored every FP32 buffer. Export plus full readback took 819 seconds and restore took 444 seconds; peak process memory was 138.316 GB. It was not model training. Eight streams remain prospective for the production trainer and require its own resource admission; E11 uses four.
Resource reservations alone do not prove peak-memory fit. Miners must follow
the approved source and signed epoch manifest; GitHub preparation does not
activate a new live contract.

E11 freeze optimization: at most four bounded commitment-document GETs
run concurrently. Each document remains capped at 65,536 bytes; heavy rollout
ZIPs are not prefetched. Snapshot journals, conditional copies and final
receipt publication remain serialized. The original signature, upload-window,
artifact-hash and conditional-copy checks still apply. This does not establish
a measured freeze time for a fully populated epoch and does not activate a
different live submission deadline.

Hourly commitment reads use a separate storage client with a five-second
connect timeout, ten-second socket-read timeout and one transport attempt.
Timeouts preserve completed snapshots and remain infrastructure failures, not
fraud. The cutoff stops new reads; it is not a guarantee that every network
operation has stopped at that exact instant.

The active E12 upload-only-independent-full-v1 policy removes the trainer's redundant
full optimizer-shard GET. Trainer receipts explicitly report local SHA checks
and completed uploads, not verified durable readback. This signed policy is
valid only with a qualified reader on a different physical machine performing
full GET and SHA checks for every shard. Checkpoint byte staging overlaps that
readback; checkpoint and optimizer authority publication wait for its validated
original request, signed receipt and successful terminal result. Rewards still
wait for durable training publication. Default historical export behavior is
unchanged. See docs/UPLOAD_ONLY_INDEPENDENT_STATE_READBACK.md on GitHub; this
policy is live in E11, but a completed one-hour epoch is not yet demonstrated.

Prospective registration optimization on GitHub main: fixed-block commitment,
UID and reverse-hotkey maps returned the same 246 activated identities in
16.5 seconds versus 101.9 seconds for serial lookups. Signature checks and
snapshot semantics are unchanged. E11's sealed source does not contain this
optimization; adoption requires a future signed source and epoch boundary.
See docs/BATCHED_FIXED_BLOCK_REGISTRATION_SNAPSHOT.md.

Public machine-readable endpoints /llms.txt, /mining.json, /network-data.json
and /reward-policy.json allow normal CLI GET/HEAD requests. The affine.io
Cloudflare rule skips only Browser Integrity Check on those exact public
paths; it does not grant storage credentials or upload access. Read the signed
manifest for miner-specific capabilities and current deadlines.
